subject: Finexus production: 5xx burst during peak + autoscale lag
messages:
From: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@finexus.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: support@finexus.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production spike: 5xx/429 burst during peak window

Team —

We started to see a massive spike in 5xx and 429 responses around 08:50 PT. Latency jumped to 2.1s p95 for short requests, and many of our clients experienced timeouts. The attached error_rate_sparkline.png shows the sudden burst.

Impact: several downstream services are failing, retries are amplifying traffic. We already opened a PagerDuty for this (PD-982134).

Can you confirm whether this is a capacity/autoscale issue on your side or something in our integration? We need a concrete mitigation plan and ETA — this is affecting our enterprise customers.

Thanks,
Carlos
Head of Platform — Finexus

Attachments: error_rate_sparkline.png
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@finexus.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:28:10 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production spike: 5xx/429 burst during peak window

Carlos —

Thank you for flagging this and sharing the graph. We're actively investigating. Initial signal from ops: a Dedicated pool serving Finexus experienced rapid token-level queueing during a concurrent traffic surge; autoscaler did not spin up capacity fast enough leading to brief GPU saturation and 5xx bursts.

Immediate actions we are doing now:
- Marissa is running live pool metrics and will post a short dump (attached as dedicated_pool_metrics_excerpt.csv).
- We have suspended non-critical background jobs in the affected region to free headroom.
- Rachel is opening an expedited rolling fallback to a compatible lighter-quantized model variant to reduce per-token compute while we stabilize.

I will stay on this thread with updates every 30 minutes. We understand the customer impact and will share an ETA for full remediation within the next hour.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:05:34 -08:00
Subject: Internal: Metrics dump + quick triage notes

Attaching the short metrics excerpt from the Dedicated pool that handled Finexus traffic. Quick notes:
- Node saturation at ~08:47–08:52 PT, average GPU util jumped from 58% to 98% in <=3 minutes.
- Autoscaler target added nodes at 08:54 but nodes only became ready at 09:00 (image bootstrap + model warmup).
- Error pattern: predominantly 5xx internal server errors and some 429s as ingress queue backed up; retry amplification visible in client logs.

I recommend immediate mitigations: 1) pin a lighter model variant (Rachel is on it), 2) enable short-term permissive fallback (route ~20% traffic to hosted fallback pool), 3) add a temporary upstream retry budget to reduce aggressive client retries.

Attachments: dedicated_pool_metrics_excerpt.csv, support_log_excerpt.txt

-marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: rachel_kim@redwood.ai
To: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@finexus.com>, markus_klein@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:17:50 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production spike: 5xx/429 burst during peak window

Carlos —

We pushed a temporary model-variant fallback at 11:12 PT that reduces per-token GPU time by ~28% on your workload profile; this has already reduced error rates in the last 10 minutes. We also applied an ingress token-based concurrency cap to limit immediate queueing.

Observed: 5xx rate dropped ~70% over the 11:12–11:22 window; latency p95 improved to 1.0s. We continue to monitor for retried requests creating secondary spikes.

Next steps planned:
- Full capacity rehydration: we are accelerating image warmup and will pre-warm additional Dedicated nodes for the remainder of the peak. ETA: 45–60 mins.
- Config change: a short-lived soft retry budget recommended for your SDK (guidance pasted below) to prevent amplification.

Quick retry guidance for Finexus SDK: set max_retries=3 with exponential backoff starting at 100ms and max_backoff=1.5s. If you prefer, we can deploy a per-account server-side short-circuit to cap retry bursts.

We will continue posting updates.

— Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Product Manager, Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@finexus.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 15:43:00 -08:00
Subject: Incident summary and exec note — Finexus 5xx burst (final update)

Carlos / team —

Final update and executive summary for your post-mortem.

What happened: during Finexus's 08:45–09:05 PT peak, a sudden traffic surge caused the Dedicated GPU pool to saturate. The autoscaler reacted but new nodes were not ready fast enough (image bootstrap + model warmup delay), causing transient 5xx/429 bursts. Client retries then amplified the load.

Mitigations applied:
- Immediate: model-variant fallback and ingress concurrency cap (11:12 PT) — reduced error rate by ~70%
- Short term: pre-warm additional Dedicated nodes and disabled non-critical background jobs (11:30 PT)
- Account-level: enabled server-side retry throttling option for Finexus to limit aggressive retries

Permanent actions we will propose:
- Autoscaler improvements: faster node readiness via lightweight warm snapshots and prioritized model warmup for pinned customers
- Deployment: a standby warm pool for high-SLA Dedicated customers to eliminate bootstrap latency during peaks
- SDK guidance: safer retry defaults and client-side jitter/backoff docs (we'll coordinate with your SDK team)

Attachments: error_rate_sparkline.png, dedicated_pool_metrics_excerpt.csv, support_log_excerpt.txt

If you want a brief exec-level call, Markus and I are available this afternoon at 3:30 PT. Otherwise we'll send a formal RCA and a remediation timeline within 48 hours.

Appreciate your patience — we're treating this as a priority.

Best,
Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
